description: Single-panel quantitative line plot (Fig. 3). The linear y-axis is labelled "Intragranular κ-carbide size / nm" and spans 0 to 30 in increments of 5 nm; the x-axis is labelled "Aging temperature / °C" with three plotted positions at 550, 600 and 650. One data series is shown: grey filled squares joined by a straight line, each carrying a vertical error bar (mean ± standard deviation), identified in the legend at lower right as "Aged for 6 h". Reading against the gridlines, the square at 550 °C lies just above the 10 nm line, the square at 600 °C lies between the 15 and 20 nm lines (closer to 20), and the square at 650 °C lies just below the 25 nm line; the error bars are small and of similar length at all three temperatures. No numeric data labels are printed on the panel, so exact means and standard deviations cannot be read from the pixels. The figure demonstrates that the equivalent-circle-diameter size of intragranular κ-carbide precipitates increases monotonically and roughly linearly with aging temperature between 550 and 650 °C after 6 h of aging. It is a standalone statistical summary panel containing no micrographs, spectra or maps.

Shows a monotonic increase of κ-carbide size with aging temperature.

observations.observation: The panel is a single line plot with three grey square markers joined by a straight line, each marker carrying a vertical error bar, and a legend at the lower right reading "Aged for 6 h".
The y-axis is labelled "Intragranular κ-carbide size / nm" and is linear from 0 to 30 with gridlines/ticks every 5 nm.
The x-axis is labelled "Aging temperature / °C" with exactly three plotted data positions at 550, 600 and 650.
The data point at 550 °C lies just above the 10 nm gridline of the y-axis.
The data point at 600 °C lies between the 15 and 20 nm gridlines, closer to 20 nm.
The data point at 650 °C lies just below the 25 nm gridline.
The κ-carbide size increases monotonically with aging temperature from 550 to 650 °C, and the error bars are short and of similar length at all three temperatures.
No numeric data labels are printed anywhere on the panel; only axis ticks and the legend text are legible, so the exact mean and standard-deviation values cannot be read off the image.
The caption states that the figure plots the size of intragranular κ-carbide precipitates as a function of aging temperature after 6 h of aging, with data presented as mean ± standard deviation.
The citing text states that the 550-6 sample contains a high density of nanoscale κ-carbides of ~11 nm with rectangular morphology.

The citing text states that the intragranular κ-carbides in the 600-6 sample coarsen to ~18 nm and evolve into larger rectangular parallelepipeds in arrays along the orthogonal <100> directions of the matrix.

The citing text states that increasing the aging temperature to 650 °C coarsens the intragranular κ-carbides to approximately 24 nm in the 650-6 sample, accompanied by more pronounced intergranular precipitation.
The citing text states that the size of intragranular κ-carbides is quantified using an equivalent-circle diameter, and the quantitative evolution with aging temperature is summarised in Fig. 3.
The citing text identifies the alloy studied as Fe-30.5Mn-8Al-1C (wt%).
